directAnswer: Blessed Urban V was Guillaume de Grimoard, a Benedictine abbot who was elected on 28 September 1362 without being a cardinal and reigned until 19 December 1370. He returned the papacy to Rome in 1367, received the Byzantine emperor's personal profession of faith there, and founded and supported universities, but went back to Avignon shortly before his death. Pius IX beatified him in 1870.

paras: Guillaume de Grimoard was born at the castle of Grizac in the region of Lozère in southern France. He became a Benedictine monk, studied and taught canon law at Montpellier, Toulouse, Paris and Avignon, and served as abbot of Saint-Germain at Auxerre and then of Saint-Victor in Marseille. He was on a diplomatic mission in Naples when the cardinals, unable to agree on one of their own, chose him in 1362.
As pope he kept the Benedictine habit and the rhythm of monastic life. He reduced the luxury of the court, opposed the accumulation of benefices, and pressed for the reform of clergy and religious.

Urban was deeply committed to education. He supported large numbers of poor students at his own expense, endowed colleges at Montpellier, and approved the founding of universities at Kraków in 1364 and Vienna in 1365, among others. He also encouraged missionary work in eastern Europe and Asia.

His reign coincided with crusading expeditions to the eastern Mediterranean, including the sack of Alexandria by King Peter I of Cyprus in 1365 and the campaign of Count Amadeus VI of Savoy in 1366, which Urban encouraged as responses to Turkish and Mamluk power.

Against the wishes of most of his French cardinals, Urban left Avignon and entered Rome in October 1367, the first pope to reside there in some sixty years. He began restoring its neglected churches, and in 1368 he placed the relics venerated as the heads of Sts. Peter and Paul in new reliquaries at the Lateran. Emperor Charles IV visited him in 1368.
In 1369 the Byzantine emperor John V Palaiologos came to Rome and made a personal profession of the Catholic faith before the pope, though it did not bring about a union of the churches.

Instability in the Papal States and war between France and England led Urban to return to Avignon in September 1370, despite appeals to remain, including from St. Bridget of Sweden. He died there on 19 December 1370, only months after his arrival. His remains were later moved to the abbey of Saint-Victor in Marseille.
Miracles were reported at his tomb, and his reputation for holiness grew. Pope Pius IX beatified him in 1870.

keyFacts: Born Guillaume de Grimoard at Grizac, France; Benedictine abbot of Saint-Victor, Marseille
Elected in 1362 though not a cardinal
Supported poor students and the founding of the universities of Kraków and Vienna
Returned to Rome in 1367; received John V Palaiologos's profession of faith (1369)
Went back to Avignon in 1370 and died there on 19 December 1370

faqs.question: Did Urban V move the papacy back to Rome?
faqs.answer: He resided in Rome from 1367 to 1370, the first pope to do so in decades, but returned to Avignon in 1370. The lasting return came under his successor, Gregory XI, in 1377.

faqs.question: Why is Urban V a Blessed?
faqs.answer: He was known for his holy, monastic way of life and concern for the poor and for students, and miracles were reported at his tomb. Pope Pius IX beatified him in 1870.

faqs.question: Which universities did Urban V help found?
faqs.answer: He approved the founding of the universities of Kraków (1364) and Vienna (1365), and he supported colleges and poor scholars at Montpellier and elsewhere.
